assumptions: The root state name `ABSHydraulicRegulator` is synthesized from the natural-language system description because no summary field or SpecJson root name was provided.
The initial state is chosen as `increase` because it is the first state named in the natural-language state list and no hierarchy or initial-state override was provided.
The continuous PID slip computation and plant dynamics are outside this discrete FSM model; `slp` is represented as an external float input used by the transition guards.

grounding_seeds.evidence_text: single-wheel ABS hydraulic regulator as a three-state FSM
transition guards split the slip-error space into four bands using `slp` thresholds

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init verifies the initial transition enters increase and applies the increase valve and pump outputs
scenario_results.name: default_init_enters_increase

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes increase -> hold exactly at slp=0.01 and checks hold neutralizes both valves
scenario_results.name: increase_to_hold_at_positive_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start no-fire probe verifies increase does not transition to hold when slp is just above 0.01
scenario_results.name: increase_stays_above_positive_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes hold -> increase when slp is greater than 0.01 and checks increase output commands
scenario_results.name: hold_to_increase_above_positive_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start boundary no-fire probe verifies hold does not transition to increase at slp=0.01
scenario_results.name: hold_stays_at_positive_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes hold -> decrease when slp is less than -0.01 and checks pressure-release outputs
scenario_results.name: hold_to_decrease_below_negative_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start boundary no-fire probe verifies hold does not transition to decrease at slp=-0.01
scenario_results.name: hold_stays_at_negative_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes decrease -> hold exactly at slp=-0.01 and checks hold neutralizes pressure-release outputs
scenario_results.name: decrease_to_hold_at_negative_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start no-fire probe verifies decrease does not transition to hold when slp is just below -0.01
scenario_results.name: decrease_stays_below_negative_boundary

evidence: DSL states: increase, hold, decrease under ABSHydraulicRegulator.
increase enter assigns k1=1, k2=0, n=0; hold enter assigns k1=0, k2=0, n=0; decrease enter assigns k1=0, k2=1, n=500.
DSL guards match NL: increase->hold slp <= 0.01, hold->increase slp > 0.01, hold->decrease slp < -0.01, decrease->hold slp >= -0.01.
GroundingMap marks all states, variables, actions, transitions, and guards as required with high confidence.
findings.summary: The DSL is faithful to the core NL discrete supervisor: it contains the required three states, the specified valve/pump entry actions, and the four stated slip-error threshold transitions.

evidence: inspect_model_to_json_summary metrics: n_states_leaf=3, n_transitions_normal=5, n_variables=4, action_count=3.
sim_summary: 9 scenarios run and 9 passed.
Scenario set covers initialization, positive boundary, negative boundary, transition firing, and no-fire cases.
findings.summary: Coverage of the discrete FSM component is strong: required states, transitions, guards, and output actions are present and exercised by simulation scenarios.

evidence: NL: "Wheel speed and vehicle speed are used to compute the slip ratio, and the PID output drives the Stateflow supervisor".
DSL declares only slp, k1, k2, and n; no wheel-speed, vehicle-speed, slip-ratio computation, PID state, or PID output variable is modeled.
GroundingMap assumption: "The continuous PID slip computation and plant dynamics are outside this discrete FSM model; slp is represented as an external float input used by the transition guards."
findings.summary: The DSL does not explicitly model wheel speed, vehicle speed, slip-ratio computation, or PID output; these are abstracted into the external guard variable slp. This is acceptable for the stated discrete-supervisor slice but limits full-paper/system coverage.

evidence: NL includes both a PID-based slip controller and a concrete three-state Stateflow supervisor.
DSL only implements the supervisor and uses slp directly in guards.
design_diagnostics_summary external_input_role_ledger identifies slp as an external input candidate.
findings.summary: The model intentionally reduces the coupled PID/supervisor architecture to a threshold-based FSM over slp. This is not a blocking defect because the NL also says continuous dynamics remain in the plant model, but the abstraction should be documented as a scope limitation.

evidence: design_diagnostics_summary ok=true with blocking_count=0 and advisory_count=8.
W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR for slp is mitigated by nl_external_input_vars=["slp"].
W_UNREFERENCED_VAR for k1, k2, and n is consistent with NL describing these as valve/pump outputs.
findings.summary: Advisory diagnostics are expected for this abstraction: slp is externally supplied, and k1/k2/n are output variables rather than guard-driving internal variables.

evidence: warning_budget_exhausted is empty.

No transition effect or artificial slp update was introduced.
findings.summary: No unjustified warning fix is evident; the model preserves the externally-driven slp abstraction instead of adding ungrounded updates solely to silence diagnostics.

evidence: All high-confidence GroundingMap required elements are represented in the DSL.
